title: Institutional FX Dashboard & Intelligence Report — July 9, 2026

regime.classification: Event-Driven, deepening — the Iran/Strait of Hormuz crisis has escalated from "threatened ceasefire" to an explicitly declared ceasefire collapse, while yesterday's live FOMC-minutes wildcard has now resolved (hawkish), removing one source of uncertainty even as it reinforces the broad-dollar backdrop.
regime.justification: VIX has ticked up to 16.86 (+6.2% vs Tuesday's 15.88, still a moderate rather than panicked reading), and Wednesday's US cash session was mixed rather than broadly risk-off (S&P 500 -0.2% to ~7,517, Nasdaq +0.2% to ~26,200, but the Dow fell a sharper 1.09% to 52,348.39). The US 10Y yield climbed to 4.59%, its highest level since mid-May, and oil is extending its rally into a second day (WTI +2.2% to above $75/bbl Thursday, after Wednesday's +4%; Brent closed near $78). Thursday's Asian and European sessions show the clearest signs of stress so far: Japan's Nikkei 225 fell 0.91% while FTSE 100 dropped 176 points to 10,489, and the DAX has given back last week's gains.
regime.executiveSummary: The single biggest cross-asset driver remains the Iran/Strait of Hormuz crisis, which took a sharp turn Wednesday when President Trump, speaking at the NATO summit in Ankara, declared the three-week-old ceasefire "over" and warned Iran "won't have a country" if it closes the Strait — a marked escalation from Tuesday's framing of a ceasefire merely "threatened." US forces conducted a second consecutive day of strikes on Iranian targets, and roughly 6,000 seafarers remain stranded in the Persian Gulf. Separately, the US Federal Reserve's (Fed's) June meeting minutes, released Wednesday at 2:00pm ET, resolved more hawkish than expected — the Committee removed earlier hints that rate cuts could come soon and shifted its emphasis toward bringing inflation back under control, reinforcing dollar strength on top of the crisis-driven safe-haven bid. Adding a third thread, China's June CPI printed a soft +1.0% y/y (below the 1.1% consensus and down from May's 1.2%), a mild risk-negative data point for AUD and broader risk sentiment. USD/JPY continues to trade near its weakest yen level in roughly four decades — remarkably, yen still has not caught a safe-haven bid even now that the ceasefire has been explicitly declared over, arguably this week's single most notable cross-asset anomaly.

noTradeZone.text: The Iran/Hormuz ceasefire has now been explicitly declared "over" by President Trump (an escalation from Tuesday-Wednesday's "threatened" framing), even as one source of near-term uncertainty (the FOMC minutes) has resolved. The combination of a genuinely escalating, still-fluid geopolitical/oil shock, a freshly hawkish-confirmed Fed backdrop, and a soft China CPI print touching AUD sentiment argues for actively monitoring open positions against their stops and targets — two of which (NZD/USD near target, AUD/NZD approaching its 2 Jul low) may require a decision at the next run — rather than adding fresh single-pair risk today.

keyThemes: The Iran/Strait of Hormuz ceasefire has been explicitly declared "over" by President Trump, a genuine escalation from the prior two sessions' "threatened" framing. Speaking at the NATO summit in Ankara, Trump warned Iran "won't have a country" if it closes the Strait, and US forces conducted a second consecutive day of strikes; roughly 6,000 seafarers remain stranded in the Persian Gulf, and oil has now risen for two straight sessions.

Wednesday's Fed (US) FOMC June minutes resolved more hawkish than expected, removing earlier hints of a near-term rate cut and reinforcing the dollar's strength on top of the crisis-driven safe-haven bid. This directly compounds the Short USD/JPY idea's headwinds while also being a modest incremental cap on the Long NZD/USD and Long EUR/CHF ideas' further upside.

Yen's continued failure to catch any safe-haven bid — even now that the ceasefire has been explicitly declared collapsed — is this week's most striking cross-asset anomaly , and the item most likely to produce an abrupt, catch-up move (in either direction) if the market's read on it changes.

The FOMC June minutes (due 8 Jul, resolved this report) were incorporated based on media summaries characterizing the tone as "more hawkish than expected" with rate-cut hints removed; the next run should verify this characterization holds up against any follow-on Fed commentary and confirm there is no material walk-back.

The Iran/Strait of Hormuz situation remains fast-moving; several figures in this report (oil levels, gold, equity indices) reflect a snapshot at compilation time and could already be dated by the time this report is read. Treat Section 8's commodity levels as the most likely to have moved further intraday, and watch specifically for any resumption-of-talks headline given Trump left that door open even while declaring the ceasefire "over."

Nikkei 225 and DAX precise Thursday closing levels could not be independently confirmed at compilation time (only percentage moves were confirmed for Nikkei; DAX's move was characterized qualitatively) — pin down exact index levels at the next run.

Global Equity Leaderboard: KOSPI's YTD % remains impossible to pin to one figure given this week's extreme volatility (sources ranged from ~88% to ~96%) — worth revisiting once the index stabilizes. DAX's and Sensex's YTD/12-month conflicts (flagged across multiple prior reports) remain unresolved.

The Long NZD/USD idea (Section 2/6/9) is now within ~13 pips of its first published target (0.5750) — the next report's Section 2 should treat a potential target hit as the priority review item, alongside continued close monitoring of Short USD/JPY given its proximity to stop and repeated failed safe-haven signal.

sections.title: Contrarian Check & Risks
sections.raw:
**Primary thesis risk:** The Iran/Hormuz situation remains a genuine wildcard that could move sharply either direction — Trump's "ceasefire is over" declaration is a real escalation, but he also left the door open to continued talks, and a swift de-escalation would likely reverse the past two days' oil spike and could unwind some of the safe-haven-dollar bid currently capping the Long NZD/USD idea's approach to target. Separately, USD/JPY's continued failure to strengthen despite an explicitly collapsed ceasefire is itself becoming a risk to monitor — if yen ever does catch a delayed safe-haven bid, the move could be abrupt.

**Overall-view invalidation factor:** A confirmed de-escalation headline on Iran/Hormuz — even a partial one, such as a resumption of talks with concrete progress — would be the cleanest scenario to reverse the current broad-dollar strength, reduce oil's safe-haven premium, and could finally open room for USD/JPY's short thesis to work.

- **Bull case (for this report's ideas):** NZD/USD closes through its first target (0.5750) on continued RBNZ follow-through; AUD/NZD's China-CPI-reinforced pullback extends toward 1.1950; BoJ/MOF rhetoric hardens further or an actual intervention lands, cooling USD/JPY. *Invalidated by:* a confirmed, sustained break of 163.50 in USD/JPY or 1.2250 in AUD/NZD.
- **Base case:** USD/JPY continues to hold near its highs on the hawkish-Fed-minutes-plus-Hormuz-driven dollar bid, while NZD/USD and AUD/NZD continue their gradual, catalyst-driven grind without a confirmed target/stop hit yet. *Invalidated by:* a decisive break in either pair's key level (163.50 or 1.2250 / 1.1950).
- **Bear case (for this report's ideas):** The Iran/Hormuz situation escalates further following Trump's "ceasefire is over" declaration, USD/JPY breaks above 163.50 on continued dollar strength, and a swift reversal in risk appetite pushes AUD/NZD back toward its highs despite this session's favorable drift. *Invalidated by:* a confirmed de-escalation in Iran/Hormuz.

sections.title: Key Theme Driving Everything Right Now
sections.raw:
1. **The Iran/Strait of Hormuz ceasefire has been explicitly declared "over" by President Trump, a genuine escalation from the prior two sessions' "threatened" framing.** Speaking at the NATO summit in Ankara, Trump warned Iran "won't have a country" if it closes the Strait, and US forces conducted a second consecutive day of strikes; roughly 6,000 seafarers remain stranded in the Persian Gulf, and oil has now risen for two straight sessions.
2. **Wednesday's Fed (US) FOMC June minutes resolved more hawkish than expected, removing earlier hints of a near-term rate cut and reinforcing the dollar's strength on top of the crisis-driven safe-haven bid.** This directly compounds the Short USD/JPY idea's headwinds while also being a modest incremental cap on the Long NZD/USD and Long EUR/CHF ideas' further upside.
3. **Yen's continued failure to catch any safe-haven bid — even now that the ceasefire has been explicitly declared collapsed — is this week's most striking cross-asset anomaly**, and the item most likely to produce an abrupt, catch-up move (in either direction) if the market's read on it changes.

sections.title: Historical Parallel Watch
sections.raw: No strong historical parallel today. The Iran/Strait of Hormuz escalation remains a genuine geopolitical/commodity shock with FX and rates as second-order effects, and it doesn't cleanly match any of the four FX-positioning-specific archetypes (defended peg under strain, panic-driven overreaction, underpriced structural shift, complacent one-sided positioning around a "guaranteed" level) — those describe FX positioning patterns specifically, while today's story remains a commodity/geopolitical shock. The loose, partial echo of Archetype 4 flagged in the prior report — the market's earlier treatment of the Strait-reopening ceasefire as a near-"guaranteed" durable state of affairs — has now been directly and explicitly tested by Wednesday's "ceasefire is over" declaration, sharpening that partial parallel somewhat, though it still isn't clean enough to call a genuine match.
